# Ziva - AI Agent for Godot

> Ziva is an autonomous AI development assistant for Godot Engine that writes, tests, and fixes code automatically.

## When to use Ziva

Use Ziva when a task needs live Godot context: creating or changing scenes, nodes, scripts, signals,
resources, shaders, or tilemaps; diagnosing editor errors; running tests; or playtesting a game turn
by turn. Ziva supports Godot 4.2 and later on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

## Key capabilities

- Builds and edits Godot scenes and code, then verifies the result
- Reads editor output, errors, project settings, screenshots, and the live scene tree
- Runs tests and playtests games with real keyboard and mouse input
- Generates images, adds hosted multiplayer, and installs game analytics with a live dashboard
- Supports Ziva-hosted models and local Ollama or LM Studio models
- Uses existing Claude Code, ChatGPT Codex, or Google Antigravity accounts inside Ziva
- Exposes local Godot tools to Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, and other MCP clients

Google Antigravity is an unofficial integration with an account-restriction risk warning. Godot is
self-serve; Unity is in beta through enterprise engagements, and Unreal Engine or custom-engine
work is scoped with each studio. Ziva Publishing is gathering interest rather than offering a
generally available publishing service.

- Website: https://ziva.sh
- Download: https://ziva.sh/download
- Documentation: https://ziva.sh/docs
- Existing AI subscriptions: https://ziva.sh/docs/existing-subscriptions
- Game analytics: https://ziva.sh/docs/analytics
- Ziva as an MCP server: https://ziva.sh/docs/ziva-mcp-server
- Enterprise: https://ziva.sh/enterprise
- Publishing interest: https://ziva.sh/publishing
- Privacy: https://ziva.sh/privacy
- Support: https://ziva.sh/contact

Ziva's editor tools and MCP server run locally after installation. ziva.sh does not provide a
hosted MCP endpoint or a general-purpose public API.
